fact: The Eswatini Revenue Service says customs payments made through FNB Eswatini now show almost instantly on ASYCUDA, so traders can process their customs declarations more quickly.
The Eswatini Revenue Service says customs payments through FNB now reflect in near real time in its ASYCUDA customs system, completing the integration on 12 June 2026.
Trade Minister Manqoba Khumalo says a National Single Window System is under development to digitise customs procedures, with border posts at Mananga, Ngwenya and Lavumisa being upgraded.

The Eswatini Revenue Service says in a 3 February 2025 presentation that customs declaration data is automatically exchanged with the South African Revenue Service, and that it built its electronic certificate of origin on existing ASYCUDA World infrastructure.

Times of Eswatini, reading the Eswatini Revenue Service 2024/25 annual report, says ERS made continued upgrades to ASYCUDA World for customs operations during 2024/25, with system availability averaging 99.9 per cent.
The World Customs Organization says on 18 October 2024 that the Eswatini Revenue Service runs an ASYCUDA World Risk Management Module, to be upgraded in 2025.

The Eswatini Revenue Service says ASYCUDA World, a web-based customs management system, lets traders submit declarations online and file before reaching the border, and announced an upgrade so clients can declare from their own business systems.
